introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0750 Geography 1, JUNE 2023, ADVANCED LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one hour 30 minutes. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed 'Advanced Level - 0750 Geography 1'; fill in the information required on the answer sheet (Candidate Name, Exam Session, Subject Code and Candidate Identification Number). Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is correct, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet, using the blank spaces. At the end of the examination the invigilator collects the answer sheet first and then the question booklet. The paper has two sections: Section A, Physical Geography (questions 1 to 25), and Section B, Human Geography (questions 26 to 50).

questions.enonce_markdown: The layers of the atmosphere in sequence from the earth's surface upwards are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The atmosphere is divided into layers according to the way temperature changes with height. Starting at the ground the order is: **troposphere** (where weather occurs, temperature falls with height), **stratosphere** (contains the ozone layer, temperature rises with height), **mesosphere** (temperature falls again, the coldest layer) and **thermosphere** (temperature rises strongly with height). Only option C lists the four layers in this order; the other options mix up the sequence.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Isolate the non-solar energy depletion process in the atmosphere from the following list:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The incoming solar radiation (insolation) is reduced (depleted) on its way through the atmosphere by three processes: **absorption** (by water vapour, ozone, carbon dioxide and dust), **reflection** (mainly by clouds) and **scattering** (by gas molecules and dust particles). **Condensation** is the change of water vapour to liquid water droplets. It releases latent heat and forms clouds, but it is not a process that removes energy from the incoming solar beam. It is therefore the odd one out.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the condensation product is associated with a convective precipitation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Convective (convectional) precipitation results from strong heating of the ground, rising of warm moist air, cooling, condensation and the growth of large towering clouds. The condensation product (cloud) associated with it is the **cumulonimbus**, the tall thunder cloud that gives heavy showers, thunder and lightning, typical of the equatorial belt in the afternoon. Altocumulus and stratocumulus are layered or lumpy sheets of middle or low cloud that give little or no heavy rain. Convectional rainfall is the precipitation itself, not the condensation product (the cloud).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A relationship of high annual temperature and low annual precipitation is exhibited in which of the following climatic regions in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
High temperatures with low annual rainfall characterise the **dry tropical (Sudanian and Sahelian) climate** of the northern part of Cameroon (Adamawa, North and Far North), with a long dry season, a short rainy season and annual rainfall that decreases northwards toward Lake Chad. The Guinean (equatorial) climate of the south, the Cameroon type climate of the Western Highlands and the Cameroon maritime climate of the coast are all wet climates with high annual rainfall.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The Cameroon type of climate prevailing in parts of the Coastal Lowlands and Western Highlands with very high annual rainfall amounts (2000mm - 4000mm) is respectively influenced by any one of the following combination of factors.

*Options as printed:* A) Relief and convection   B) Relief and Monsoon winds   C) Monsoon winds and Relief   D) Monsoon winds and convection
questions.corrige_markdown:
The very high rainfall of the Cameroon type climate (Mount Cameroon slopes, coastal lowlands, the south-western flanks of the Western Highlands) is mainly relief (orographic) rainfall: the moist south-west monsoon winds blowing in from the Atlantic are forced to rise over the highlands, cool, condense and give heavy rain. So the two factors are **relief and the monsoon winds**. Convection plays only a minor role in this wettest sector, which excludes options A and D.

Options B and C are printed with the same two factors in a different order ("Relief and Monsoon winds" and "Monsoon winds and Relief"), so the printed key cannot be told apart from the other and the item is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: B (Relief and Monsoon winds).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 1 below is a graph, showing conditions of annual soil moisture budget for a tropical region.

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

*Figure 1: Soil moisture conditions (moisture in mm against months J to D, with the precipitation curve and the potential evapotranspiration curve). Source: Adapted from Nchangvi S.K (2008) P. 133.*

Identify the soil moisture conditions at (a).
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a soil moisture budget, precipitation is compared with potential evapotranspiration (PET, the water the plants and the air could use if water were unlimited). At (a), from January to about April, the precipitation curve lies **below** the PET curve, so water demand is greater than supply. As the soil store has already been used up, the vegetation lacks water: this is a **soil moisture deficit** (the hatched area between the two curves). Surplus would be shown where precipitation exceeds PET and the soil is full (the area above the PET curve in the wet season), recharge where precipitation exceeds PET while the soil store is being refilled (the rising limb in April), and utilization where precipitation is below PET but the soil store is still being drawn on (the dry-season fall of the curve from August to November).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The major rivers that drain into Lake Chad drainage basin are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lake Chad is the centre of an inland (endoreic) drainage basin. In the Cameroon, Chad and Central African Republic sector its main feeders are the **Chari and its tributary, the Logone**, which flow from the south through the Chadian lowlands (the Chari alone supplies most of the water of the lake). The Benue (with its tributary the Faro) flows west into the Niger and then to the Gulf of Guinea, and the Sangha flows south into the Congo basin, so they do not drain to Lake Chad.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What are the key aspects of the river basin that are affected by human activities?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for the aspects (characteristics) of the basin that are changed, not for the human activities themselves. Urbanization (A), irrigated agriculture (B) and deforestation (D) are all human activities. The aspects of the river basin that they alter are the **runoff, the discharge of water and the transport of load** (for example, paved surfaces and deforestation increase runoff and flood peaks, and more sediment is carried).

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Urbanization especially the paved surfaces, roofs and drains
Agriculture especially irrigation, rice and sugar cane cultivation
Runoff, water discharge and load transport
Deforestation especially of the river catchment and the surrounding forests

questions.enonce_markdown: The Mantle is different from the Crust because it is a constitution of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The mantle lies between the crust and the core (about 2900 km thick). It is made of hot, dense silicate rocks rich in iron and magnesium that behave as a **semi-solid, slowly flowing (plastic) material**, and it is heated by the core and by radioactive decay, which drives the convection currents that move the plates. Granitic and metamorphic rocks rich in silica and aluminium (B, the sial) form the continental crust, basaltic rocks (C, the sima) form the oceanic crust, and the liquid nickel-iron (D) is the outer core.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Rocks in semi-solid state of silicate minerals and generate heat.
Granitic and Metamorphic rocks rich in silica and aluminium.
Basaltic rocks rich in silica and magnesium.
Rocks in liquid state of Nickel and Iron in very high temperature.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following characteristics best suits plate margins of divergence?
questions.corrige_markdown:
At divergent (constructive) margins, such as the mid-Atlantic ridge and the East African rift, plates move apart and basaltic (basic, low-silica, runny) magma rises. The eruptions are therefore **quiet (effusive)**, the lava is **basic**, and the earthquakes are weak and **shallow-focus**, with tension (normal) faults. Option A (tear faults) describes conservative margins, B (deep focus, acidic lava) and C (compressional faults, violent eruptions) describe convergent margins.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Tear faults violent volcanic eruptions and basic lava
Quiet volcanic eruptions, deep focus earth quakes and acidic lava
Shallow focus earth quakes violent volcanic eruptions and compressional faults
Basic lava, quiet volcanic eruptions shallow focus earthquake

questions.enonce_markdown: In the occurrence of volcanism, only one of the processes represent all the activities involved.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Volcanism (vulcanicity) covers all the movement of molten rock (magma) from the interior into the crust and onto the surface. It has two parts: **intrusive** activity, where magma is injected into the crust (dykes, sills, batholiths), and **extrusive** activity, where magma is ejected onto the surface (lava flows, ash, volcanoes). Only B covers both. A covers only the extrusive part, C only the intrusive part, and D is wrong because the epicentre is the point on the surface above an earthquake focus, not the source of magma.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Magma reaches the earth's surface as lava before cooling and solidifying.
Magma is injected into the crust or ejected onto the surface.
Volcanoes are formed from molten rocks injected into the crust
Magma flows from an epicenter to form volcanoes.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following crater lakes is not located along the Cameroon Volcanic Line?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Cameroon Volcanic Line is the chain of volcanic mountains and crater lakes that runs from the Gulf of Guinea (Mount Cameroon, Manengouba, Bamenda Highlands, Oku) to the north-east. The twin Manengouba lakes and Lake Oku lie in volcanic craters on the line, and Lake Barombi (Barombi Mbo, near Kumba) is a crater lake in the south-western part of the line. **Lake Ossa**, near Edea in the Littoral Region, is a coastal lake in the Sanaga lowlands that is not a volcanic crater lake on the line.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following represents processes of chemical weathering?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Chemical weathering changes the chemical composition of rock minerals, usually with water. **Hydration** (minerals take up water and swell) and **hydrolysis** (water reacts with minerals such as feldspar to form clay) are chemical processes, which are very active in hot, wet climates like southern Cameroon. Thermal expansion and contraction, exfoliation, thermal shattering, frost action and crystal (salt) growth are physical (mechanical) weathering processes.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A greater part of a river's load is transported through which of the following mechanisms?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A river carries its load by solution (dissolved material), suspension (fine silt and clay held up in the flowing water), saltation (sand and fine gravel bounced along the bed) and traction (large stones rolled or dragged along the bed). In most rivers the finest particles are carried in **suspension** over long distances and make up the largest part of the load, mainly during floods, whereas traction and saltation move only the coarse part. (In limestone areas the dissolved load can be greater, but suspension is the general answer.)

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which are the main inputs in a coastal system?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The coast is an open system. Its **inputs** are **energy** (waves, tides, currents and wind) and **materials** (sediments brought by rivers, by cliff erosion and from the sea bed, plus shells and other remains of dead marine animals). Processes such as erosion and transportation (B, C) are the movement of materials within the system, not inputs; in D, "wave action" is a form of energy and "sediments" and "beach materials" repeat the same input. Option A is the only one that names energy and materials with no process included.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Energy, sediments, shells of dead sea animals

questions.enonce_markdown: The constituents of soil are: mineral matter, organic matter, air and water. In a soil profile which one of the above soil constituents makes up a greater portion of the soil?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A typical mineral soil is made of about half solid material and half pore space. In the solid part, **mineral matter** (particles of sand, silt, clay from the weathered parent rock) is by far the largest component, about 45 per cent of the soil volume by the usual textbook figure, whereas organic matter is only a few per cent. Air and water together fill the pore spaces (about half of the volume), but each one separately is smaller than the mineral matter.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The physical and chemical characteristics of the soil are determined by one of soil forming factors.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The soil forming factors are parent material, climate, relief, organisms (biological activity) and time. The **parent material**, the weathered rock or deposit from which the soil develops, determines the mineral content, the texture, the structure, the permeability and the nutrient reserves, that is the basic physical and chemical characteristics of the soil. Climate, organisms and time modify the soil, and climate in particular controls the rate of weathering and leaching, but the characteristics inherited from the rock are those given by the parent material.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Isolate the pedogenic regime associated with areas characterized by mean annual temperature of about 28°C and annual rainfall of more than 1500mm.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A pedogenic regime is the main soil-forming process of a climatic region. In the hot, wet tropics (mean temperature about 28°C and rainfall above 1500 mm), chemical weathering and leaching are intense: silica and bases are washed out and iron and aluminium oxides accumulate. This process is **ferrallisation** (laterisation), which gives the red ferrallitic soils (latosols) of southern Cameroon. Calcification occurs in semi-arid grasslands, salinization in dry areas with strong evaporation, and gleization in permanently waterlogged soils.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Choose the soil types that are found on the Western Highlands of Cameroon from the following:

*Options as printed:* A) Ferrugenous, volcanic, alluvial   B) Scree, alluvial, volcanic   C) Podzol, latosol, volcanic   D) Meadow, volcanic, latosol
questions.corrige_markdown:
The soils of the Western Highlands of Cameroon are formed mainly on volcanic rocks (basalts and ash), under a cool, wet climate. The characteristic soils are the **young fertile volcanic soils** (andosols), the **ferrallitic soils or latosols** on older surfaces and on lower slopes, and mountain (meadow-type) soils on the high plateaus. Podzols (C) form in cool, wet climates on acid sand and are not typical of Cameroon, and ferruginous soils (A) belong to the drier Sudano-Sahelian north. Scree is a rock debris on steep slopes rather than a soil type, and alluvial soils are limited to the valley floors.

Because options B and D both contain acceptable elements, the question is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: D (Meadow, volcanic, latosol).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Nutrient cycling here is characterised by a fairly small biomass store, smaller litter store, while the soil store is by far the largest. Nutrient transfer is greater from biomass to litter, followed by litter to soil. The transfer from soil to biomass is the least. The above relates to which of the following
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is the description of Gersmehl's nutrient cycling model. In **temperate grasslands** the grasses form a small biomass store and a small litter store (the dead material decomposes quickly), whereas the deep humus-rich soil holds most of the nutrients, so the soil store is by far the largest. Transfers from biomass to litter and from litter to soil are large, and the uptake from soil to biomass is small. In the tropical rain forest most nutrients are in the biomass and the litter store is small, and in coniferous forests the litter store is large because the needles decompose slowly.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Plant succession takes a long time to evolve and follow stages. Select the correct sequence from the following:

*Options as printed:* A) Pioneer, invasion, adaptation, climax   B) Colonization, invasion, competition, dominance   C) Pioneer, invasion, elimination, migration   D) Colonization, migration, adaptation, glaciation
questions.corrige_markdown:
Plant succession is the orderly change of vegetation over time, from a bare surface to a stable climax community. The standard stages are: **nudation and colonization** by pioneer species, **invasion** (migration and establishment of new species), **competition** between the species and their effect on the habitat, and finally **stabilization with the dominant climax species**. Of the printed sequences, B is the one whose steps follow this order (colonization, invasion, competition, dominance). C and D contain steps that are not stages of a succession (elimination, migration as a final step, glaciation), and A gives a similar list with a vague stage ("adaptation").

Because A and B both resemble the usual sequence, the printed key is not certain.

**Intended answer: B (Colonization, invasion, competition, dominance).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A vegetation with a great diversity of plant species relate to which of these types in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Biodiversity is greatest where the climate is hot and wet all year round. The **tropical (equatorial) rainforest** of the south of Cameroon (for example the Congo-basin forests of the East and South Regions and the coastal forests) has the highest diversity of plant species, with several hundred species per hectare in many tree layers. The Guinea, Sudan and Sahel savannas have fewer species, because the dry season grows longer and the rainfall lower towards the north.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these measures can be used to combat drought?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Drought control combines measures that save water and protect the vegetation and the soil: **tree planting** (afforestation, shelter belts), **reduced grazing**, **alternative energy** (to reduce the cutting of trees for fuelwood) and **water conservation**. The other options include harmful practices (overgrazing, overhunting, deforestation, over-cultivation, pollution) which cause or worsen drought and desertification.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Tree planting, reduced grazing, alternative energy, water conservation
Cloud seeding, overgrazing, overhunting, tree planting
Irrigation, dam construction, deforestation, over cultivation
Tree planting, deforestation, pollution, over cultivation

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the agent of pollution responsible for the leaching of important soil nutrients like calcium and potassium and killing fish.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Acid rain** is rain made acid by sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the burning of fossil fuels and from industry. It leaches (washes out) the nutrient cations such as calcium and potassium from the soil, which then becomes less fertile, and it makes lakes and rivers acid, which kills fish and other aquatic life. Solid waste, oil spillage and nitrogenous waste (fertiliser run-off, which causes eutrophication) pollute in other ways and do not leach calcium and potassium by acidity.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Invisible drought occurs when:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Droughts are classified into permanent (arid areas with no season of enough rain), seasonal (a regular dry season), contingent (rain irregular and unreliable) and **invisible drought**. The invisible drought occurs even in humid and sub-humid areas, where the total rainfall seems adequate, when the daily supply of soil moisture does not equal the daily water need of the plants (evapotranspiration), so that crops suffer a hidden water stress. A is a description of normal rain in humid areas, B describes a seasonal drought and C a permanent drought.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: In the humid and sub-humid areas, the rain falls over a period of time
The dry season is extended in areas of distinct wet and dry seasons.
In the arid areas, no season has precipitation to satisfy the water needs of plants
The daily supply of soil moisture fails to equal the daily water needs of plants

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 2 illustrates the relationship between population density and altitude.

![fig-2](gce-al-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

*Fig 2: The relationship between population density and Altitude (height in metres against population density per km², with a thin curve for the theoretical world situation and a thick line for real world situations).*

What is the reason that best explains the increase in population density between 500m and 1250m?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In theory, population density falls steadily as altitude rises (thin curve), because it gets colder, the soils are thinner and communications are harder. In the real world (thick line), the density **increases** between about 500 m and 1250 m. This happens in **low-latitude (tropical) regions**, where the lowlands are hot, humid and often unhealthy (malaria, sleeping sickness), so people prefer the cooler, healthier, more fertile highlands, as in the Western Highlands of Cameroon, the East African highlands or the Andes. High altitudes above about 2500 m are then too cold again and the density drops. Options B and D describe cold lowlands in high latitudes, which would put people in the lowlands, and C is not a reason for dense settlement at moderate altitude.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Such regions are in low latitude areas where low altitude is too hot for human habitation.
Such regions are in high latitude areas where low altitude are too cool for human habitation
Such areas are in dry desert environments where low altitudes are too hot for human habitation.
Such areas are in the mid-latitudes where the snow covers low altitude areas

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the population data in Table 1 for countries L, M, N and O.

**Table 1: Population data in millions**

| Country | Youth | Adults | Aged |
|---|---|---|---|
| L | 13 | 31 | 17 |
| M | 19.5 | 32 | 14 |
| N | 16 | 29 | 14 |
| O | 15 | 20 | 10 |

Which of the countries L, M, N, and O has the highest dependency ratio?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The dependency ratio compares the dependants (the young and the aged) with the economically active adults:

$$\text{dependency ratio} = \frac{\text{youth} + \text{aged}}{\text{adults}} \times 100$$

- L: $(13 + 17)/31 \times 100 = 96.8$
- M: $(19.5 + 14)/32 \times 100 = 104.7$
- N: $(16 + 14)/29 \times 100 = 103.4$
- O: $(15 + 10)/20 \times 100 = 125.0$

Country **O** has the highest ratio: there are 125 dependants for every 100 adults. The trap is to pick M, which has the largest number of young people but also many adults.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 3 below shows the Demographic Transition Model. On the figure, line b represents?

![fig-3](gce-al-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

*Source: Adapted from Nagle G. & Spencer K. (2001), p. 97.*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the demographic transition model, the birth rate and the death rate are both high and fluctuating in stage 1. In stage 2 the death rate (solid line, a) falls first, while the birth rate stays high (the dotted line, b, stays at the top until the end of stage 2), then in stage 3 the birth rate (b) falls steeply and joins the low death rate in stage 4. The line that remains high through stage 2 and falls in stage 3 is the **birth rate**. The thick rising S-shaped curve (c) is the total population, and the gap between the birth and death rates is the natural increase.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the population data for countries H, I, J and K in the table below and answer question 29.

| Country | Total population in million | Death in million | Births in millions | Pop growth rate in % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H | 20 | 5 | 2 | 2.8% |
| I | 15 | 3 | 1.8 | 3.1% |
| J | 25 | 4.5 | 2.1 | 1.5% |
| K | 18 | 3.5 | 2.2 | 2.0% |

Using the law of 70 (average life expectancy), which of the countries labeled H, I, J, and K has the lowest doubling time?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The "rule (law) of 70" gives the time a population takes to double:

$$T_{double} = \frac{70}{\text{growth rate (\%)}}$$

- H: $70/2.8 = 25.0$ years
- I: $70/3.1 = 22.6$ years
- J: $70/1.5 = 46.7$ years
- K: $70/2.0 = 35.0$ years

The shortest doubling time belongs to the country with the highest growth rate, **I** (about 22.6 years). The birth and death columns are not needed, and they are not consistent with the growth rates printed in the last column (the printed deaths exceed the births), so the growth-rate column is the one to use.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
"The volume of migration is inversely proportional to the distance travelled by migrants" This law is often attributed to who?

*Options as printed:* A) E.G. Ravenstein   B) Everett Lee   C) Hornby and Jones   D) G.K. Zipf
questions.corrige_markdown:
The statement is a distance-decay law of migration: the number of migrants decreases as the distance between the origin and the destination increases, because the cost, the risk and the lack of information grow with distance. It comes from **E.G. Ravenstein's laws of migration** (1885), who observed that most migrants travel only short distances. Everett Lee is known for the push-pull model with intervening obstacles, and G.K. Zipf for the inverse-distance and rank-size ideas, which also relate migration to distance, so the attribution in the printed question is not unique.

**Intended answer: A (E.G. Ravenstein).**

questions.enonce_markdown: Increase population necessitates increase production of food. This describes:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Thomas Malthus (1798) argued that population grows in a geometric progression (1, 2, 4, 8) whereas food production grows only in an arithmetic progression (1, 2, 3, 4), so population growth will always overtake the food supply unless checked by positive checks (famine, disease, war) or preventive checks. The idea that a rising population requires more food and is limited by it is therefore the **Malthusian theory**. Boserup (C) argued the reverse, that population pressure forces farmers to intensify and raise food production, the exponential model (B) describes the growth curve itself, and the gravity model (D) describes interaction between places.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "The population problem is not caused by the rapid growth rate of population but rather by the mal-distribution of resources." This view is strongly supported by
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Karl Marx** rejected Malthus's view. For him, poverty, hunger and "overpopulation" are caused by the unequal ownership and distribution of resources and wealth in a capitalist system and not by the number of people. Malthus (A) saw population growth outrunning food, Boserup (C) saw population growth as a stimulus to agricultural innovation, and Alfred Weber (D) is the author of the theory of industrial location.

**Answer: B.**

**Shifting cultivation** is the type in which farmers clear and burn a patch of forest or bush, grow a mixture of crops (mixed cropping) for a few years using the natural fertility of the soil with no fertiliser and only simple tools, then move to a new plot when yields fall. It needs very large areas of land per family and is possible only where the population density is very low. Bush fallowing is similar but the farmers return to the same plots after a fallow period, so it needs less land, and subsistence and peasant farming are general terms that do not describe the movement and the very extensive land use.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the economic rent using the formula ER/LR = Y(m-c-td) for a particular crop cultivated on a piece of land, the yield (Y) is 115 tonnes per unit of land, with the market price (m) of 1375 francs per tonne, production cost (c) is 195 francs per tonne, transport cost (t) per km is 100 francs per tonne and the distance (d) is 25km.

*Options as printed:* A) 108,125   B) 106,950   C) 125,000   D) 209,000
questions.corrige_markdown:
The formula is the von Thunen economic rent (location rent) formula, $ER = Y(m - c - td)$, where $Y$ is the yield, $m$ the market price per unit, $c$ the production cost per unit, $t$ the transport cost per unit per km and $d$ the distance to the market.

With the values printed in the question ($Y = 115$, $m = 1375$, $c = 195$, $t = 100$, $d = 25$):

$$ER = 115 \times (1375 - 195 - 100 \times 25) = 115 \times (1375 - 195 - 2500) = 115 \times (-1320) = -151\,800 \text{ francs}$$

This value is negative (the crop is grown beyond the margin of cultivation) and **it is not one of the four options**. Option B (106,950) is obtained only if the transport cost for 25 km is 250 francs, that is $t = 10$ francs per km: $115 \times (1375 - 195 - 250) = 115 \times 930 = 106\,950$. The printed data and the options are therefore inconsistent and the question is left open.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which are the handicaps to industrialization in the developing countries?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The main obstacles to industrial growth in developing countries are the shortage of capital, small domestic markets (low incomes and small populations), a lack of skilled labour and know-how, poor infrastructure and political instability. Option A lists only genuine handicaps. B includes "high technology", which is a benefit, C includes "good transport", and D includes "large markets", so those three options contain items that are not handicaps.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the figure 4 below showing Weber's locational triangle with two sources of raw materials (Rm₁ and Rm₂), a market (m) and production point (P), and answer the question that follows.

![fig-4](gce-al-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

*Figure 4: Weber's locational triangle (market M at the top, raw material sources RM₁ and RM₂ at the base, and four possible plant sites P₁, P₂, P₃ and P₄, with P₃ at the centre and P₄ on the line between P₃ and M).*

If a manufacturer uses 400,000 tonnes and 350,000 tonnes of raw materials to produce 950,000 tonnes of manufactured products, where would the manufacturing plant be located with regards to Weber's locational triangle above?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Weber's theory the plant is located where transport costs are lowest, which depends on the weight of the materials moved. Here the total weight of raw materials is $400\,000 + 350\,000 = 750\,000$ tonnes and the weight of the product is $950\,000$ tonnes. The material index is $750\,000 / 950\,000 \approx 0.79$, which is less than 1, so the process is weight-gaining (other materials such as water are added) and the product is heavier and costlier to transport than the raw materials. The plant is therefore pulled towards the **market M**, to the site nearest to it, **P₄**. P₃ would be the site if the weights were balanced, and P₁ and P₂ are pulled towards the raw material sources, for weight-losing processes.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Table 2 is a presentation of forms of transport and terminal costs.

**Table 2: Forms of transport and terminal costs**

| | Forms of transport | Terminal costs |
|---|---|---|
| i | Road | Low |
| ii | Rail | Higher |
| iii | Air | Very high |
| iv | Water | Highest |

Which of the following is an appropriate description of the relationship in (ii)?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Terminal costs are the costs of loading, unloading, handling and storing goods at the start and end of a journey. For rail (ii) they are relatively high because railways need **complex terminal facilities** (stations, goods yards, marshalling yards, cranes) and goods often have to be transhipped to and from road vehicles. Road transport has low terminal costs because of its simple facilities and ease of loading (this is option B, which describes (i)). Option D describes the line-haul (running) costs, which are the costs while moving, not the terminal costs, and C is a different problem.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The complex terminal facilities and transshipment cost.
The simplicity of terminal facilities and the ease of loading and unloading.
Poorly developed networks that cause delays
High costs of maintenance, depreciation fuel and wages.

questions.enonce_markdown:
It is an index which compares the observed or actual number of circuits in a network with the maximum possible number of circuits in the network and usually expressed as a percentage. This can be expressed by the formula: $a = (e-v+1/2v-5) \times 100$

This description refers to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **alpha index** measures the connectivity of a network as the ratio of the actual number of circuits to the maximum number of circuits possible, as a percentage:

$$\alpha = \frac{e - v + 1}{2v - 5} \times 100$$

where $e$ is the number of edges (links) and $v$ the number of vertices (nodes). The cyclomatic number ($e - v + 1$) is only the actual number of circuits (the numerator), the beta index is $e/v$ (links per node) and the gamma index is $e/(3(v-2))$ (the ratio of actual links to maximum possible links).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "Agricultural activities in Cameroon are dominated by subsistence agriculture and employ over 70% of the active peasant population". Isolate the characteristics of subsistence agriculture from the following;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Subsistence agriculture produces food mainly for the farmer's own family, on small plots, with simple tools (hoe, machete), family labour, little capital and few fertilisers, and often with several crops grown together (multiple or mixed cropping). Option A gives exactly these features. B (exports, large capital, large farms), C (high use of fertiliser, large markets) and D (large plots, mechanization, large capital) describe commercial agriculture.

questions.enonce_markdown: The most economical form of transport of heavy bulky goods over long distances is by
questions.corrige_markdown:
For heavy, bulky and low-value goods (ores, oil, timber, grain, containers) moved over long distances, **water transport** (sea and inland waterways) has the lowest cost per tonne-kilometre: ships carry very large loads for a small amount of fuel and need no costly track to maintain. Its terminal costs are high, but they are spread over the long distance. Rail is the next cheapest, road is costly over long distances and air is the dearest and is used for light, valuable and urgent goods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If a rural population in the northern part of Cameroon is seeking a site to settle, which of the following pair of factors would be considered most important?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The northern part of Cameroon has a dry tropical (Sudano-Sahelian) climate with a long dry season, and the people there depend on livestock and on crops. The site factors that matter most in such a dry area are **water** (rivers, wells, boreholes, waterholes) and **grazing land** for the herds. Defence was important in the past on hill sites, and building materials are generally available locally, so they are secondary, and arable land alone does not solve the problem of water supply.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Nearest Neighbour Index (Rn) for a rural settlement is calculated and the Rn value is 2.15. What would be the description for this rural settlement pattern?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The nearest neighbour index ranges from 0 to 2.15. A value of **0** means a completely clustered (nucleated) pattern, a value of about **1** a random pattern, and the maximum value of **2.15** a **perfectly regular (uniform)** pattern, where the settlements are spaced evenly in a hexagonal lattice. Values between 1 and 2.15 tend towards regularity, but 2.15 exactly is the perfect regular pattern.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are some of the ways that villages adapt to their physical environment: wide verandas, thatch roofs, large windows and short houses. This relates to which of the following areas?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Wide verandas give shade and keep the rain off the walls, thatch roofs are cool and shed heavy rain, and large windows allow the air to circulate, so the house stays cool and ventilated. These features are used in **hot humid areas**, for example the forest villages of southern Cameroon. In hot dry areas houses have small windows and thick walls to keep out the heat, and in cold areas they have thick walls and small windows to keep the warmth in.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
From Figure 5, what relationship exists between population size and number of functions?

questions.enonce_markdown:
According to the rank size rule, the hierarchy of towns in Cameroon is represented by which of the following patterns?

*Options as printed:* A) Primary pattern   B) Stepped order pattern   C) Binary pattern   D) Primate pattern
questions.corrige_markdown:
The rank-size rule (Zipf) states that the population of the nth largest town is 1/n of that of the largest. Urban hierarchies are described as primate (one town far larger than all the others), rank-size, stepped order or binary patterns. Cameroon has **two dominant cities, Douala and Yaounde**, of broadly comparable size, followed by much smaller towns, which is why textbooks describe its hierarchy as a **binary pattern** (the main contrast with a primate pattern, where there is only one dominant city).

The key is a textbook classification that depends on the source, so the question is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: C (Binary pattern).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study Figure 6 below showing one of Christaller's hexagonal network.

![fig-6](gce-al-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

*Fig 6: Christaller's hexagonal network (a central place at the centre of a hexagon, with smaller settlements around the hexagon).*

The K-value represented by the hexagonal network in the figure above is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Christaller's central place theory, the K-value is the number of smaller market areas served by a central place of a higher order (including its own). With the settlements at the six corners of the hexagon, each corner is shared by three neighbouring hexagons, so each contributes one third of its area to the central place:

$$K = 1 + 6 \times \tfrac{1}{3} = 3$$

This is the **marketing principle (K = 3)**. For the traffic principle the settlements lie at the middle of the sides, each shared by two hexagons, so $K = 1 + 6 \times \tfrac{1}{2} = 4$, and for the administrative (separation) principle the six lower-order places lie wholly inside the hexagon so $K = 1 + 6 = 7$.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The original role of green belts is to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A green belt is a ring of protected open land (farmland, woodland, parks) around a built-up area, where building is restricted. It was introduced mainly to **control urban sprawl**, that is to stop the outward growth of the city and the merging of neighbouring towns, as in the London green belt. The other options (improved environment, recreation) are benefits that came afterwards, and urban renewal and preservation of architecture are matters concerning the inner city.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following measures will bring in much revenue to a country as a result of trading with other countries?

*Options as printed:* A) Quotas   B) Exchange Control   C) Trade agreement   D) Tariffs
questions.corrige_markdown:
Quotas (limits on the quantity of imports), exchange control (limits on the foreign currency available) and tariffs (taxes on imports) are trade barriers meant to restrict imports and to protect local industry. A **trade agreement** (bilateral or within a trade bloc) opens markets and lowers barriers, which increases exports and imports and so the revenue that a country earns from trade. Tariffs do give the government some customs revenue, but they reduce the volume of trade, so the question can also be read in favour of D, and the printed key is not certain.

**Intended answer: C (Trade agreement).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The main reason why developing countries accept foreign aid is to:

*Options as printed:* A) increase savings gap   B) reduce foreign exchange gap   C) reduce export revenue gap   D) reduce technical gap
questions.corrige_markdown:
Developing countries have too little domestic saving to finance investment (the savings gap) and too little foreign currency to pay for imported machinery, fuel and technology (the foreign exchange gap, or trade gap), and they also lack technical skills. Foreign aid (grants, soft loans, technical assistance) is accepted to **fill or reduce** these gaps. Option A is worded as "increase" the savings gap, which is wrong (the aim is to reduce it), and C is not a gap that aid is meant to fill. B (foreign exchange gap) and D (technical gap) are both real aims of aid, so the question has no single sure key.

**Intended answer: B (reduce foreign exchange gap).**
